topic: Ventilation: Modes of mechanical ventilation in children (VC, PC, PRVC, SIMV, PSV)

slides.title: Ventilator modes, finally simple
slides.subtitle: VC, PC, PRVC, SIMV & PSV for paeds PGs

slides.title: 3 questions behind every mode
slides.subtitle: Answer these and any mode makes sense
points: **Trigger**: what starts the breath? Machine **time** or patient effort (**pressure/flow**)
**Target**: what does the machine control? **Volume** or **pressure**
**Cycle**: what ends inspiration? **Time**, volume or a **fall in flow**
**Sequence**: are breaths all mandatory (**A/C**), mixed (**SIMV**) or all spontaneous (**PSV**)?
slides.highlight: Mode name = control variable + breath sequence (e.g. PC-A/C, VC-SIMV)

slides.title: Volume vs pressure control
slides.subtitle: Volume control (VC) || Pressure control (PC)
points: You set **tidal volume** and flow || You set **inspiratory pressure** and Ti
Airway pressure **varies** with compliance || Tidal volume **varies** with compliance
Constant (square) flow || **Decelerating** flow, better gas distribution
Guaranteed minute ventilation || Caps peak pressure, copes with **ETT leak**
Risk: high pressures if lungs stiffen || Risk: low Vt if compliance falls
slides.highlight: Watch the variable you did NOT set: pressure in VC, tidal volume in PC

slides.title: PRVC: the hybrid
slides.subtitle: Pressure-regulated volume control
points: You set a **target tidal volume**; each breath is delivered as a **pressure-controlled** breath
Machine adjusts the pressure **breath by breath** to reach the target (within a set limit)
Gives **decelerating flow** plus a **volume guarantee**
Pitfall: if the child pulls hard, the machine **lowers support**: watch for fatigue
A large **ETT leak** makes measured Vt, and so PRVC, unreliable
slides.highlight: Neonatal cousin: volume-targeted ventilation (volume guarantee, VG)

slides.title: A/C vs SIMV
slides.subtitle: Assist-control (A/C) || SIMV
points: **Every** breath fully supported; set rate is the minimum || Only the **set number** of breaths fully supported
Extra patient breaths get the full set breath || Extra breaths are spontaneous, usually with **PS**
Risk: over-ventilation, **auto-PEEP** if tachypnoeic || Risk: more **work of breathing** if PS too low
Best for the sick, sedated child || Weaning by SIMV is **slower** than PS / SBT

slides.title: PSV: the patient leads
slides.subtitle: Pressure support ventilation
points: **Every breath patient-triggered**; machine adds a set pressure above PEEP
**Flow-cycled**: inspiration ends when flow falls to ~25% of peak (adjustable)
Child controls **rate, Ti and Vt**: the most comfortable mode
No mandatory rate, so it needs an intact **respiratory drive** + apnoea backup
Used for weaning and SBTs (CPAP + low PS, e.g. **5-10 cmH2O**)
slides.highlight: Red flag: no drive = no breaths on PSV. Always check apnoea backup

slides.title: Choosing a mode at the bedside
points: Sick, sedated or paralysed: **A/C** (PC or PRVC)
Stiff lungs / PARDS: **Vt 5-8 mL/kg** ideal body weight, **Pplat ≤28 cmH2O** (PALICC-2)
Big ETT leak or air leak: favour **pressure control**
Good drive and improving: move to **PSV**, then an **SBT**
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: the mode matters less than the Vt, pressures and PEEP you set

Ventilator modes confusing you on PICU rounds? 🫁

Every mode is just 3 questions: what triggers the breath, what the machine controls, and what ends inspiration.
VC vs PC, the PRVC hybrid, A/C vs SIMV and PSV, all in 8 slides.
Plus a bedside cheat-sheet with PALICC-2 lung-protective targets.
